findings.title: Same-name declaration exempts a provider-internal xs_call lifecycle
findings.input_state: The client sends native x_search plus a top-level function declaration named x_keyword_search. xAI emits a provider-internal item shaped as {type:function_call, call_id:xs_call_internal, name:x_keyword_search} at output_index 0.
findings.wrong_behavior: isInternalCall asks the declaration table to match the response item and returns false as soon as the same-name top-level function is found. It does not recognize the evidenced xs_call provider-internal identity. The output_item event is therefore emitted instead of recorded as dropped; associated argument delta/done and output_item.done events also remain visible, response.completed retains the item through the same predicate, and later visible indices are not compacted for that trace.
findings.expected_behavior: The provider-internal xs_call lifecycle must be suppressed even when a client declaration reuses its short name; a legitimate client call with the declared identity must remain visible.
findings.reproduction: An independent temporary unit test on the reconstructed result tree failed with: provider-internal xs_call trace leaked because a client declaration reused its name. The returned event was {"type":"response.output_item.added","output_index":0,"item":{"id":"internal_1","type":"function_call","call_id":"xs_call_internal","name":"x_keyword_search","arguments":"{}"}}.
findings.test_gap: internal/runtime/executor/xai_executor_test.go:457-529 covers an undeclared custom_tool_call and a differently qualified declared tool, but not a provider-internal xs_call function_call colliding with a same-name top-level declaration.

tests.tree: reconstructed result plus temporary review-only test
tests.output: provider-internal xs_call trace leaked because a client declaration reused its name

review_summary: Evidence hashes, exact scope, forward/reverse application, six-predecessor prepared tree, result tree, and mandated suites all reproduce. The slice is rejected because xAI search classification ignores the provider-internal xs_call identity when a same-name top-level declaration exists, exposing the complete internal lifecycle and preventing required index compaction.
